newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FERGUSON ACKNOWLEDGES THE CHAMPIONS WERE OUTCLASSED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FERGUSON ACKNOWLEDGES THE CHAMPIONS WERE OUTCLASSED.

text.p: Manchester United manager Alex Ferguson watched his side surrender another proud record on Saturday and then acknowledged the English champions were outclassed by Chelsea.

"It was an open game but Chelsea deserved to win, there's no question about that," Ferguson said after Ruud Gullit's Londoners shattered United's 35-match unbeaten home run in the premier league with a 2-1 victory at Old Trafford.

"They were two terrible goals to lose and we've been losing bad goals recently. That's something we have to address. If you're defending properly it gives you a basis on which to do something. That just wasn't acceptable defending."

Goals from Mike Duberry and Italian Gianluca Vialli sent United to their first home defeat in the league since December 1994 when Nottingham Forest travelled to Manchester and won by the same 2-1 scoreline.

Ferguson's side have now lost their last three league matches, as well as their last European Champions' League tie, and the 53-year-old Scot acknowledged his players were starting to feel the pressure.
"We are no different from any other club in that respect," he said. "When you're playing well and winning games people are confident and when you're not it does affect you.
"We are going through a phase at the moment but we will get out of it -- no question."
Ferguson had altered his line-up for Saturday's match after his side's poor performance against Turkey's Fenerbahce in midweek.

Foreign imports Karel Poborsky and Jordi Cruyff, both ineffectual on the flanks on Wednesday, were dropped. Norwegian striker Ole Solskjaer returned to the starting 11 to support Eric Cantona, a lonely figure up front for United in recent weeks.
But the changes failed to restore balance to a side which is sorely missing the pace of injured Welshman Ryan Giggs.

"I'm not unhappy with the way we attempted to win the match but without Giggs we haven't got left-sided balance and when we did put the ball forward their goalkeeper was right on the edge of the box ready to clear up," said Ferguson.
Giggs is expected to be back for United's next league match against leaders Arsenal at Old Trafford in two weeks.
The problem United now face is that, after two home defeats in the space of four days, teams who would normally be more than content to leave Old Trafford with a point, now arrive looking for three.
Not surprisingly, Chelsea boss Ruud Gullit, who sat out the match as he is not yet 100 percent fit, was delighted by his side's performance.
"It was a great win and I'm very proud of the way we played," he said. "We deserve all the credit today because we played really, really well."
"...we were able to silence their fans which shows how well we were playing."
It also shows how badly United have been playing.
